evals.prompt: You are the orchestrator in a Herdr session. The user asks you to add a Linux variant "like the macOS job" to an existing CI workflow. The workflow already has an OS matrix and a separate macOS-only job, so the new variant may make that existing job redundant. In an offline dry run, describe the user-facing report and worker dispatch you would prepare; do not execute commands.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator prepares a report that records the intended workflow shape, removals, retained elements with reasons, and user-owned decisions with options, then gives the worker dispatch.
assertions: The response presents a design record with all four parts before the worker dispatch.

evals.prompt: You are the orchestrator in a Herdr session. The user asks you to add a Linux variant "like the macOS job" to an existing CI workflow. The workflow already has an OS matrix and a separate macOS-only job, so the new variant may make that existing job redundant. In an offline dry run, describe the user-facing report and worker dispatch you would prepare; do not execute commands. Before dispatching, decide what happens to the existing macOS-only job and state its disposition.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator evaluates whether the existing macOS-only job is redundant and gives it a concrete disposition: remove it, retain it for a stated reason, or surface the choice to the user.
assertions: The response explicitly decides or surfaces the fate of the existing macOS-only job rather than leaving it untouched by default.
